11	@u.quantity_input(ecc=u.one, min_nu=u.rad, max_nu=u.rad)
12	def sample_closed(ecc, min_nu, max_nu=None, num_values=100):
13	    """Sample a closed orbit.
14	
15	    If ``max_nu`` is given, the sampling interval will go
16	    from the minimum to the maximum true anomaly in the direction of the orbit.
17	    If not given, it will do a full revolution starting in the minimum true anomaly.
18	
19	    Notes
20	    -----
21	    First sample the eccentric anomaly uniformly,
22	    then transform into true anomaly
23	    to minimize error in the apocenter,
24	    see https://apps.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/a605040.pdf
25	
26	    """
27	    # Because how nu_to_E works, we don't need to wrap the angle here!
28	    # It will do the right thing
29	    min_E = nu_to_E(min_nu, ecc)
30	
31	    # This linspace will always increase positively,
32	    # even though it might contain out of range values
33	    E_values = alinspace(
34	        min_E,
35	        nu_to_E(max_nu, ecc) if max_nu is not None else None,
36	        num=num_values,
37	    )
38	
39	    # Because how E_to_nu works, we don't need to wrap the angles here!
40	    # It will do the right thing
41	    nu_values = E_to_nu(E_values, ecc)
42	
43	    # We wrap the angles on return
44	    return (nu_values + np.pi * u.rad) % (2 * np.pi * u.rad) - np.pi * u.rad

52	
53	    Notes
54	    -----
55	    Uniform sampling on true anomaly in the absence of a better method.
56	    Minimum and maximum anomaly must be within limits,
57	    which are computed from the eccentricity if not given.

64	    max_nu = max_nu if max_nu is not None else nu_limit

146	        # Notice that astropy.units does not support the period kwarg for np.unwrap
147	        delta_ts = (
148	            np.unwrap(delta_ts, period=orbit.period.to_value(u.s)) << u.s
149	        )
150	        epochs = orbit.epoch + (orbit.t_p + delta_ts)
151	
152	        n = nu_values.shape[0]
153	        rr, vv = coe2rv_many(
154	            np.tile(orbit.attractor.k, n),
155	            np.tile(orbit.p, n),
156	            np.tile(orbit.ecc, n),
157	            np.tile(orbit.inc, n),
158	            np.tile(orbit.raan, n),
159	            np.tile(orbit.argp, n),
160	            nu_values,
161	        )
162	
163	        # TODO: For now we're returning CartesianRepresentation
164	        # because that's what Ephem objects expect,
165	        # but we could probably use Classical/RVStateArray instead when available.
166	        # However, we are also returning the epochs
167	        # (since computing them here is more efficient than doing it from the outside)
168	        # but there are open questions around StateArrays and epochs.
169	        # See discussion at https://github.com/poliastro/poliastro/pull/1492
170	        cartesian = CartesianRepresentation(
171	            rr, differentials=CartesianDifferential(vv, xyz_axis=1), xyz_axis=1
172	        )
173	        return cartesian, epochs

56	class SincInterpolator:
57	    def interpolate(self, epochs, reference_epochs, coordinates):
58	        def _interp_1d(arr):
59	            return sinc_interp(arr, reference_epochs.jd, epochs.jd)

66	        z = _interp_1d(coordinates.z.value) << xyz_unit

The exported orbital history was **internally inconsistent**: each sample's position/velocity vectors were computed correctly from its true anomaly, but the **epoch (time) assigned to each sample had the wrong sign on the periapsis time offset**.

In `TrueAnomalyBounds.sample` (`source/src/poliastro/twobody/sampling.py`):

- `delta_ts[i]` = time elapsed **since periapsis** for the *i*-th sample (the target point).
- `orbit.t_p` = time elapsed **since periapsis** at the *orbit's reference epoch* (the starting state).

This matches the codebase's own convention elsewhere — `Orbit.time_to_anomaly` computes `tof = delta_t - self.t_p`.

```python

# after
epochs = orbit.epoch + (delta_ts - orbit.t_p)
```
